clusters.title: 87-Year-Old Woman Evicted From Madrid Home, Sparks Widespread Housing Protests
clusters.summary: Maricarmen Abascal, an 87-year-old woman, was forcibly evicted on Wednesday from her Madrid apartment, where she had lived for 71 years. Riot police clashed with demonstrators who had gathered outside the building, chanting "Maricarmen, you are not alone." Abascal was carried from the building on a stretcher and taken to Gregorio Marañón Hospital, where she is being treated for exhaustion, stress, and anxiety. She refused a free emergency placement offered by the city and is temporarily staying with a relative. The eviction followed a legal battle against a real estate firm, Urbagestión Desarrollo e Inversión S.L., which acquired her apartment and raised the monthly rent by 275% to 2,650 euros. Abascal had been paying around 500 euros a month, a figure that was almost double her monthly pension. The Supreme Court ruled in the firm's favor in March, clearing the way for the eviction. Thousands of people protested in Madrid, Barcelona, and other cities on Wednesday night, expressing outrage at the eviction and the unaffordable housing market. A protest in Madrid attracted 10,000 people, according to the central government, and began in front of a luxury penthouse recently purchased by the Madrid regional government. Protesters cried "Ayuso’s penthouse for Maricarmen!" and "Shame! Shame!" The incident has intensified a political dispute over Spain's housing policies ahead of next year's general election. Housing costs in Spain have increased sharply over the past decade, with the average price of a square meter for rent or purchase rising by around 50%. Madrid has been particularly affected, topping a world ranking for luxury properties for two consecutive years. Spain's public housing stock is limited, with only 1.2% publicly owned, a figure substantially lower than in other European countries. Residents also attribute rising prices and reduced supply to short-term tourist rentals like Airbnb.
consensus_points: Maricarmen Abascal, an 87-year-old woman, was evicted from her Madrid home on Wednesday.
The eviction followed an increase in her monthly rent by a real estate firm.
Widespread protests erupted in Madrid and other Spanish cities in response to the eviction.
The incident has highlighted Spain's ongoing housing crisis and sparked political debate.
The Supreme Court had ruled in favor of the real estate firm, allowing the eviction to proceed.
divergence_points: The Daily Mail and The Local Spain emphasize the use of riot police and clashes with demonstrators during the eviction.
El Pais (English) and The South China Morning Post provide specific details on the broader housing crisis, including statistics on rent increases and the limited public housing stock.
El Pais (English) reports that a protest in Madrid attracted 10,000 people and began in front of a controversial luxury penthouse purchased by the Madrid regional government.
Euro Weekly News details the legal history of Maricarmen's tenancy, including the challenge to her second succession by the property investment company.

clusters.title: Rome Colosseum Remains Closed After Worker Dies in Fall
clusters.summary: The Colosseum in Rome will not reopen to the public before Saturday, following the death of 22-year-old rope-access worker Andrea Moretti. Moretti died in a fall overnight between Tuesday and Wednesday while installing a new lighting system at the monument. The Colosseum closed on Wednesday as a sign of mourning and remained shut on Thursday and Friday. Culture Minister Alessandro Giuli's decision on its reopening will depend on the initial results of the investigation into Moretti's death. The minister also plans a meeting with the site's workers to assess their psychological well-being. Premier Giorgia Meloni called for the cause of Moretti's death to be fully clarified as quickly as possible, calling it unacceptable. Moretti fell approximately 10 meters, and his harness was reportedly not fastened to a rope. The Rome prosecutor’s office opened a manslaughter investigation into his death on Wednesday. Trade unions staged a demonstration outside the Colosseum on Wednesday, calling for justice for Moretti and greater health and safety in Italian workplaces. The workplace accident insurance agency INAIL reported on Tuesday that Italy registered 1,189 work-related deaths in 2025. This figure was 37 fewer than in 2024, a drop of 3.02%, but still averages over three work-related deaths every day. The monument was initially partially closed on Wednesday, with only the second level affected, but the entire site was later closed after workers' unions argued that keeping it open showed a lack of respect.
consensus_points: The Colosseum in Rome is closed following the death of 22-year-old worker Andrea Moretti.
Moretti died in a fall while installing a new lighting system at the monument.
The Colosseum will remain closed until at least Saturday.
Italy's Culture Minister Alessandro Giuli is awaiting investigation results and will meet with workers before deciding on reopening.
Premier Giorgia Meloni called for a full clarification of the cause of death.
divergence_points: ANSA (English) and The Local Italy provide specific details on the ongoing investigation and the broader context of work-related deaths in Italy, citing INAIL figures.
The New York Post and CNN focus on the temporary and rare nature of the Colosseum's closure.
ABS-CBN News and IJR (Independent Journal Review) initially reported only a section or level of the Colosseum being closed, while later articles confirmed the entire site's closure.

clusters.title: Ukraine Invasion Reduces Russia to China's Junior Partner
clusters.summary: Russia's invasion of Ukraine has reduced the country to the status of China's junior partner, according to analysis of their economic relationship. While China and Russia promote a no-limits partnership, limits are apparent in the energy sector. As Europe phases out Russian gas imports, Moscow seeks Beijing to offset the pressure, but China refuses to provide aid on terms favorable to Russia. Russian President Vladimir Putin attended the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) summit in Bishkek on August 31, hoping to discuss the Power of Siberia-2 pipeline with his Chinese counterpart. This project aims to transport up to 50 billion cubic meters of natural gas annually from Russia’s Arctic region to China, doubling existing pipeline capacity. Beijing demands low gas prices similar to Russia’s heavily subsidized domestic rate, which would leave Russia struggling to break even. Putin was unable to secure Chinese President Xi Jinping's backing for the pipeline project at the summit. Prior to a Beijing summit in May 2026, Chinese officials reportedly rejected Moscow’s pipeline proposals and asked the Russian delegation not to press the issue. China supplies over 90% of the critical technology, microchips, and precursor chemicals fueling Russia’s defense industry. Beijing also serves as Moscow’s financial lifeline, purchasing Russian crude oil and injecting tens of billions of dollars into the Kremlin’s treasury. Civilian casualties in Ukraine climbed 114% in the first half of 2026 compared to 2024 levels.
consensus_points: Russia's invasion of Ukraine has shifted its relationship with China, making Russia a junior partner.
China supplies a portion of the technology and components for Russia's defense industry.
China serves as a financial lifeline for Russia, including through crude oil purchases.
Russian efforts to secure Chinese backing for the Power of Siberia-2 pipeline have been unsuccessful due to China's demands for low gas prices.
divergence_points: The Atlantic Council focuses on the energy sector and Russia's weakened negotiating position regarding the Power of Siberia-2 pipeline.
Fox News emphasizes China's role as Russia's "arsenal and ATM," detailing the percentage of technology supplied and financial support.

The Cipher Brief discusses broader Russian hybrid attacks against European states and intelligence assessments of potential provocations against NATO, providing a wider geopolitical context beyond the China-Russia relationship.

clusters.title: United States Denies Visa to Sudan's Al-Burhan for UN General Assembly
clusters.summary: The United States denied a visa to Sudanese army commander General Abdel Fattah al-Burhan, preventing his attendance at the UN General Assembly. Al-Burhan is the President of the Transitional Sovereign Council of Sudan. A spokesperson for UN chief Antonio Guterres expressed deep concern that the visa had not been issued and stated that the UN was engaging with Washington on the matter. The US refusal to grant the visa is seen by some as stripping legitimacy from warring factions in Sudan. The incident has been described as an implosion of US-Sudan diplomacy at the UN. US Ambassador to Guyana, Nicole Theriot, explained that a visa may be placed under review when a US Government agency receives information concerning the visa holder. The legal basis for receiving a tourist or non-business visa is proving one is not an intending immigrant to the United States. The US Embassy in Guyana was not aware that the visa of High Court Judge Justice Gino Persaud was under review when he was stopped from boarding an US-bound flight. Attorney General Anil Nandlall denied any role of the Guyana Government in Justice Persaud's visa review.
consensus_points: The United States denied a visa to Sudanese army commander General Abdel Fattah al-Burhan.
The visa denial prevented Al-Burhan from attending the UN General Assembly.
A UN spokesperson expressed concern over the visa not being issued.
divergence_points: APA News (Pan-African) and EU Today directly state that the US denied the visa to Al-Burhan.
Africanews and The Africa Report highlight the UN's concern and the broader implication of "US-Sudan diplomacy implodes."
Guyana Chronicle and Caribbean National Weekly include general information about US visa review processes and a separate incident involving a Guyanese judge, which is not directly related to Sudan.

clusters.title: Türkiye Agrees to Gradual Troop Withdrawal, Hands Over Iraq Base
clusters.summary: Türkiye has agreed to a gradual withdrawal of its forces from the strategic Bashiqa-Zelikan military base in northern Iraq and will hand over its control to the Iraqi government. The agreement followed a meeting between Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York. A joint statement from their offices confirmed that Turkish forces will transfer the camp to the Iraqi federal government in accordance with the agreed-upon mechanism and timeline. In return, Iraq pledged to remove armed groups that Türkiye considers security threats from the Sinjar region in northwestern Iraq. The two leaders agreed to fully extend the authority of the Iraqi state in Sinjar and to end the presence of banned foreign armed elements. Türkiye established a military presence at the Bashiqa base in December 2015 to support operations against the ISIS group and help secure the region. The Bashiqa base, Türkiye's furthest from its border, has been a point of contention, with Iraq accusing Türkiye of violating its sovereignty due to the unilateral deployment of troops. Türkiye has long pressed Iraq to curb groups with links to the Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK) and other non-state armed groups operating in Sinjar. The Iraqi government announced earlier in September that the Sinjar Resistance Units, a Yazidi militia affiliated with the PKK, had agreed to disarm. Eligible fighters from this group are to be integrated into the Iraqi security forces. Baghdad had declared the PKK an illegal organization and banned its activities in 2024. Türkiye and Iraq also signed a comprehensive security cooperation agreement in August 2024.
consensus_points: Türkiye and Iraq reached an agreement for Türkiye to gradually withdraw its forces from the Bashiqa-Zelikan military base in northern Iraq.
The agreement was made during a meeting between Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly.
Iraq pledged to remove armed groups considered security threats by Türkiye from the Sinjar region.
Türkiye established its presence at the Bashiqa base in December 2015 to combat ISIS and secure the region.
The Bashiqa base has been a long-standing point of contention between the two countries.
divergence_points: Asharq Al-Awsat and Iraqi News highlight the agreement as enhancing Iraqi sovereignty and detail the specific commitments from both sides regarding the base and Sinjar.
The Media Line and Hürriyet Daily News provide additional context on the PKK, with The Media Line mentioning the PKK's announced dissolution in May 2025.
Hürriyet Daily News specifically mentions the Turkish Armed Forces (TSK) presence at the base started in line with an agreement with the Kurdistan Regional Government.

clusters.title: US Diplomats Ordered to Use 'Super Intelligence' Instead of 'Artificial Intelligence'
clusters.summary: The State Department's international organizations bureau has instructed its staff to stop using the term artificial intelligence and instead use super intelligence. This directive followed President Donald Trump's remarks at the UN General Assembly on Tuesday, where he announced he would officially change the name. An email sent by Michael Drager, the bureau's deputy assistant secretary, titled "Change in Nomenclature AI to SI," ordered staff to change all references in documents, positions, remarks, and press elements. Trump stated that the word artificial makes intelligence sound fake, and that it is not fake. He declared that from this point forward, all United States government documents would be changed to use super intelligence. The email, obtained by The Associated Press on Wednesday, did not indicate whether other State Department bureaus were expected to follow this directive. US representatives used the term "SI" at the UN on Wednesday. Trump has previously attempted to rename other entities during his second term, including rebranding the Gulf of Mexico as the "Gulf of America" in January 2025. In August of this year, he issued another order renaming Lake Ontario as "Lake America" amid a trade dispute with Ottawa. Neither of these name changes has been recognized by other countries, although Google and Apple updated their maps to reflect the Gulf rename. Days before his UN speech, Trump surveyed his Truth Social followers on the idea of changing AI's name, with super intelligence winning an unscientific poll.
consensus_points: President Donald Trump announced his intention to change the name "artificial intelligence" to "super intelligence."
The State Department's international organizations bureau has instructed its staff to adopt the new term "super intelligence" (SI).
Trump stated that the term "artificial" makes the technology sound "fake."
The directive applies to documents, positions, remarks, and press elements within the bureau.
divergence_points: Euronews and The Australian highlight Trump's previous attempts to rename geographical features like the Gulf of Mexico and Lake Ontario.
The Associated Press and Anchorage Daily News provide specific details about the internal State Department email from Michael Drager and its immediate implementation by US representatives at the UN.
Truthout provides context on public concerns regarding unregulated AI expansion and mentions Trump's prior social media poll on the name change.

clusters.title: China Obtains F-35 Stealth Fighter Parts After Shipment Diverted to Hong Kong
clusters.summary: China has obtained potentially sensitive components from the F-35, the US military’s advanced stealth fighter jet, after a shipment was unexpectedly diverted to Hong Kong. The parts, including an F-35 canopy and a weapons-bay door, were being shipped from Australia to the United States for inspection, repair, or disposal earlier this year. These components, manufactured by Lockheed Martin, were coated with radar-absorbing material designed to enhance the aircraft’s stealth capabilities. The US shipping giant UPS was transporting the parts from the Australian Air Force. The transport aircraft stopped in South Korea on its way to the US, after which the shipment was rerouted to Hong Kong. Chinese authorities subsequently seized the components, which have not been returned. The Pentagon’s F-35 Joint Program Office is aware of a shipment issue and is actively working with US authorities and industry partners to retrieve the components, investigate the incident, and implement safeguards. Australian Defense Minister Richard Marles confirmed that Canberra is working with the US and Lockheed Martin to examine Australia's role in the incident. Marles stressed that the missing components were not sensitive equipment. Two congressional committees are investigating the incident. The F-35 is operated by approximately 20 countries, with Australia serving as a regional hub in the Indo-Pacific for storing spare parts and maintaining F-35s for US allies. Concerns exist within US security circles that China might reverse-engineer the F-35 components to improve its own stealth aircraft, such as the J-20 and J-35. President Donald Trump, however, approved the sale of 48 F-35s to Saudi Arabia last week.
consensus_points: F-35 stealth fighter jet parts were unexpectedly diverted to Hong Kong while being shipped from Australia to the United States.
Chinese authorities have obtained these components, which include a cockpit canopy and a weapons-bay door.
The Pentagon's F-35 Joint Program Office is investigating the incident and working to retrieve the parts.
Australian Defense Minister Richard Marles confirmed Australia's involvement in the investigation but stated the components were not sensitive.
The F-35 parts are coated with radar-absorbing material designed to enhance stealth capabilities.
divergence_points: Bloomberg and India Today explicitly state that China has seized the F-35 parts, while Al Jazeera and Military.com focus on the Pentagon's investigation into the diversion.
Al Jazeera reports the incident occurred "last week," whereas Bloomberg and The Australian state it happened "earlier this year" or "months ago."
India Today and FrontPage Magazine highlight concerns that China might reverse-engineer the components to improve its own stealth aircraft.
Al Jazeera and Kyodo News mention that China's Foreign Ministry stated it was not aware of the incident.

clusters.title: Ireland Manager Hallgrimsson Calls Gaza Remarks 'Not Clever'
clusters.summary: Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson stated that the timing of his remarks regarding the war in Gaza was not clever, as his team prepares for UEFA Nations League matches against Israel. Hallgrimsson had previously said, "We're not playing with genocide, we're playing against genocide. We're playing against Israel, we're not playing with Israel." The Israel Football Association responded by accusing Hallgrimsson of stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy. Irish Prime Minister Micheal Martin defended Hallgrimsson, calling the Israel FA's remarks unacceptable. Ireland is scheduled to play Israel in Debrecen, Hungary, on September 27, and again in Backa Topola, Serbia, on October 4. The Football Association of Ireland cited operational challenges for selecting neutral venues. Over 160 Irish athletes signed an open letter urging a boycott of the matches, and protests have occurred outside the team's hotel in Dublin.

The Israel Football Association criticized Hallgrimsson's remarks.
Ireland is scheduled to play two UEFA Nations League matches against Israel on September 27 and October 4.
Neutral venues have been selected for the matches.

clusters.title: Harvey Weinstein Sentenced to 15 Years for Sexual Assault
clusters.summary: Disgraced film producer Harvey Weinstein was sentenced on Wednesday to 15 years in prison in New York for a 2006 sexual assault conviction. The sentence follows a retrial after his previous New York convictions were overturned in 2024. Haley told the court the case felt like the worst decision of my life and that the assault had a devastating effect on my life and sense of security that may never go away, calling it a life sentence. Weinstein apologized to anyone I may have hurt by my actions but maintained his innocence. Judge Curtis Farber stated Weinstein would be remembered for his films, but his legacy would pale in comparison to his crimes and becoming the literal face of the #MeToo movement. Weinstein was previously sentenced to 23 years in 2020 for assaulting Haley and actress Jessica Mann, but those convictions were overturned. In his 2025 retrial, he was convicted in the Haley case and acquitted of a charge involving actress Kaja Sokola. He has already served over six years in prison. The judge added that Weinstein's sentence will be followed by five years of supervised release and a requirement to register as a sex offender.

The victim was former TV production assistant Miriam Haley.

clusters.title: Copper Prices Dip on Stronger Dollar, Chilean Supply Concerns
clusters.summary: Copper prices dipped on Thursday, September 24, with benchmark three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange falling 0.2% to $14,595 a metric ton by 1405 GMT. A stronger dollar and risk reduction ahead of a long Chinese holiday weekend weighed on sentiment. The dollar held near a two-month high, fueled by expectations of additional Federal Reserve interest rate hikes. A stronger US currency makes dollar-priced metals more expensive for buyers using other currencies. Worries over supply disruptions at major Chilean mines limited losses. Operations at BHP's Escondida mine in Chile, the world's largest copper mine, were suspended on Wednesday after a worker died in an accident. The LME cash copper contract premium widened to $107.5 a ton, the highest since September 1, signaling tightness for nearby supply. Capstone is focusing on Chilean copper growth. Copper is up 9% so far this quarter, having hit a record high of $14,875 a ton two weeks ago, and traded over $15,000 a tonne in London in mid-September. S&P Global projects global demand will surge from 28 million tonnes in 2025 to 42 million tonnes by 2040, boosted by demand for electric vehicles. In Zambia, Mopani Copper Mines is operating again under new Emirati owners. The mining industry accounts for 15% of Zambia's national income and 65% of exports. President Hakainde Hichilema's manifesto targets raising copper output to 3 million tonnes by 2031. Production rose from 800,000 tonnes in 2021 to just under 900,000 tonnes last year. Indian copper producers urged the government to reduce the indirect goods and services tax (GST) on copper products to 5% from 18%. The petition, sent to the GST Council on September 22, argues the current rate locks up over 490 billion rupees ($5.11 billion) in working capital. Producers committed 440 billion rupees in capital expenditure by 2030, which would create an estimated 45,000 jobs. Koryx Copper SA announced positive infill drill results at its Haib copper project in southern Namibia, with an updated mineral resource estimate and pre-feasibility study on track for publication before the end of 2026.
consensus_points: Copper prices dipped on September 24, influenced by a stronger US dollar.
Copper prices had reached record highs earlier in September, touching $14,875 a ton or over $15,000 a tonne.
Global copper demand is projected to increase by 2040, driven by electric vehicles and other transition technologies.
Zambia's mining industry is a major contributor to its national income and exports, with the country aiming to increase copper output.
Supply concerns exist, including disruptions at Chilean mines.
